regulations.title: Requirements for ME equipment and ME systems used in home healthcare environments
EMC Class B requirements for home healthcare environment
Alarm systems requirements for ME equipment and ME systems

tests.name: Mechanical Strength Test
tests.description: Additions to Table 28 Mechanical strength test of the base standard; conducted per Table 1 (non-transit-operable) and Table 2 (transit-operable)

tests.name: Mechanical Strength – Non-Transit-Operable ME Equipment
tests.description: ME equipment, parts, and mounting accessories intended for non-transit-operable use subjected to mechanical stress caused by normal use including pushing, impact, dropping and rough handling

tests.name: Shock Test (Non-Transit-Operable)
tests.description: Shock tests conducted in accordance with IEC 60068-2-27:2008

tests.name: Broad-Band Random Vibration Test (Non-Transit-Operable)
tests.description: Broad-band random vibration tests conducted in accordance with IEC 60068-2-64:2008

tests.name: Mechanical Strength – Transit-Operable ME Equipment
tests.description: Shock tests, vibration tests, and free fall tests for transit-operable equipment

tests.name: Free Fall Test (Transit-Operable)
tests.description: Per IEC 60068-2-31:2008, Procedure 1, for portable and mobile ME equipment

tests.name: Electromagnetic Emissions – Class B
tests.description: ME equipment and ME systems intended for home healthcare environment are Class B per CISPR 11:2009
tests.result_remark: Described in chapter 'ELECTROMAGNETIC COMPATIBILITY INFORMATION' of operation guide

tests.name: Alarm Systems – High and Medium Priority
tests.description: Each high priority and medium priority alarm condition causes generation of auditory alarm signals per IEC 60601-1-8:2006 and AMD1:2012, except when connected to a distributed alarm system

requirements.description: ME equipment maintained basic safety and essential performance after mechanical tests
Controls of ME equipment intended for use by a lay operator that can affect basic safety or essential performance must be protected from accidental or unauthorized changes or adjustments
Operator-adjustable controls used for calibration include a means to prevent unintentional changes from intended position
Means provided to control the risk of strangulation and asphyxiation of the patient and others to an acceptable level

review_items.description: Particular emphasis placed on the limited training of a lay operator with respect to the ability to intervene and maintain basic safety and essential performance
The manufacturer's usability engineering process included the least capable intended lay operator or lay responsible organization
review_items.result_remark: Usability was evaluated in the Usability test report

review_items.description: Usability engineering file inspected for compliance

semantic_fragments.content: Potential hazards assessed for lay operator usage: potential for improper operation or unsafe use (P); potential for confusion as to current operational mode (N/A); change in the transfer of energy or substance (N/A); exposure to environmental conditions specified in this standard (P); exposure to biological materials – No biological materials (N/A); small parts being inhaled or swallowed (N/A).

Section 10.1.3 and all sub-clauses (a, b, c, d) are marked N/A because the equipment is classified as non-transit-operable. Tests including shock tests per IEC 60068-2-27:2008, broad-band random vibration per IEC 60068-2-64:2008, and free fall per IEC 60068-2-31:2008 are therefore not required.
Section 11 (Protection Against Strangulation or Asphyxiation) is entirely marked N/A, indicating that the equipment does not present risks of strangulation or asphyxiation.

Section 13 – Additional Requirements for Alarm Systems: Each high priority and medium priority alarm condition causes generation of auditory alarm signals per IEC 60601-1-8:2006 and IEC 60601-1-8:2006/AMD1:2012, except when equipment is connected to a distributed alarm system intended for confirmed delivery of alarm conditions. Verdict: N/E. Reference: attached IEC 60601-1-8 Report.
